source.title: Capability ≠ Interpretability: Human Interpretability of Vision Foundation Models
source.authors: Julien Colin; L. Goetschalckx; Nuria Oliver; Thomas Serre

record.tranche_reason: The study tests one aspect of V5 by measuring how often SAE features match features from an independently trained SAE; it does not test the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The study uses SAE features to evaluate human interpretability, but its human localizability and semanticity results do not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical units. The feature-match rates across independent SAE seeds bear directly on the stability part of V5. The paper does not test superposition, capacity competition, or feature dimensionality.
record.test_reason: The main results are human interpretability scores, which use SAE features as a tool and do not bear on any version. Appendix F (Table A.3), however, measures how many SAE features recur in an independently seeded SAE for six vision transformers. That is a direct, if incidental, measurement of the 'stable' part of V5 in a new setting (vision models, TopK SAEs). It is closer to T3 than T2: the original source does not test SAE stability, and the study does not aim at the question.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase describes only the Appendix F robustness check, not the paper's conclusion. The authors conclude that the four foundation models (DINOv2, DINOv3, CLIP, SigLIP) have SAE features that humans find less localizable and describable than those of size-matched supervised ViTs. Interpretability is uncorrelated with downstream task performance. Feature locality and coarse-grained semantic alignment with human similarity judgments predict interpretability. Separately, they report that restricting the analysis to seed-stable features changes median localizability by at most .033 and preserves the supervised-above-foundation ordering.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses TopK SAEs and human psychophysics on vision models; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-seed match rates depend on the vision model; the study uses a cosine-similarity threshold of 0.5 to define stable features.
record.problems: The cross-seed stability assessment uses a single stated matching threshold (>0.5) and does not establish feature completeness or canonical status. The paper also notes that model-level analyses cover only six architectures.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included: the main human interpretability, capability, locality, and human-alignment results do not measure the versions in this catalog. Table A.3 also reports localizability for all features and stable-only subsets, but those scores measure interpretability rather than whether SAE features are complete or canonical units.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
All of it: no test of capacity competition or of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
All of it: polysemanticity is only asserted from citations.
All of it: no LLMs, and no measurement of features spread across neurons. SAE recovery in vision models is assumed rather than tested against an alternative.
Completeness, canonicity, and whether SAE features are the model's own units. Only cross-seed stability at one threshold, at one dictionary size, is tested.
All of it: 1-D versus multi-dimensional features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The stability numbers are a sanity check of the authors' tool, not a designed test of V5. They lack a chance baseline (e.g., a random or untrained-model dictionary), use a single 0.5 cosine threshold taken from [54], and use one dictionary size. Treat the verdicts as weak evidence on V5 stability only. The localizability columns of Table A.3 are correctly left out: they measure interpretability, not V5.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model storage of more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The claim concerns LLMs; this study examines vision models and does not measure feature spread across neurons or whether LLM features can be recovered by a dictionary.
The study tests cross-seed feature stability only. It does not establish completeness, one-to-one correspondence with canonical model units, or whether SAE features are the model's definitive units.
The study does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: ViT-S
rows.operation_detail: Matched features from the original SAE to the maximum-cosine-similarity feature in an independently trained SAE; match threshold >0.5.
rows.measure: Original features with a match in the independently trained dictionary
rows.note: The paper defines stable features as those whose maximum cosine similarity to a feature in the independent dictionary exceeds 0.5.
rows.check: Row is correct. 64.6% matched means about a third of features are seed-specific. There is no chance or random-dictionary baseline, and only one cosine threshold (>0.5) is used.

relationships.condition: CLIP ViT-B/16 and DINOv3 ViT-B/16, TopK SAE (K=38, x10 expansion), second seed, cosine >0.5
relationships.reason: Only about half of the features recur across seeds (A3-CLIP 50.1%, A3-DINOv3 50.7%), so the features are far from stable units in these models.
relationships.display_finding: Only 50.1% (CLIP) and 50.7% (DINOv3) of features had a counterpart in a second seed.

relationships.condition: ViT-S, ViT-B, SigLIP, DINOv2 under the same SAE recipe and threshold
relationships.reason: Most features recur (64.6–83.7%), but a substantial fraction does not, and stability varies by model (A3-ViT-S, A3-ViT-B, A3-SigLIP, A3-DINOv2).
relationships.display_finding: 64.6–83.7% of features recurred, leaving a substantial fraction unmatched, and stability varied by model.
